answer: Anyone may challenge a recovery by posting a bond and evidence that the request is fraudulent, which pauses the recovery until an arbiter rules. A false challenger loses the bond, so challenges stay honest, and an attacker must survive open scrutiny with proof rather than quietly seizing an account. Even a quiet reef gets heard, because recovery weighs proofs, not volume. When the beacon settles over the timber, the account stands because every recovery carried its own proof.
